title: Knowledge check: Working with v-model

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Working with v-model”?
options: Ignore rejected requests if the local form looked valid.
Bind the input to a clear state value, validate before sending, and show accessible field-specific and server-side errors.
A client-side required attribute replaces server validation.
A placeholder is a complete accessible label.
questions.answer_key: Bind the input to a clear state value, validate before sending, and show accessible field-specific and server-side errors.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Working with v-model directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Two-way binding”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
v-html is the safe default for user-generated HTML.
v-show always removes the element from the DOM.
Custom directives are the best tool for all component reuse.
questions.answer_key: Use v-if to create/remove conditional content and v-show when toggling CSS visibility is more appropriate.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Two-way binding”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Working with v-model” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
